nodes.label: Free-operator norm bound
nodes.description: For K ≥ 2 and n ≥ 1, every traceless coefficient matrix has its free-regular operator norm bounded by c(K,n) times its Hilbert–Schmidt norm. This supplies the comparison scale for the finite channel's adjoint.

nodes.label: Corrected exploration count
nodes.description: A nonempty path has at most δ + 2 important exploration times, where δ is its integer defect. Retaining the extra endpoint event repairs the count used to encode Haar trace paths.

nodes.label: Count paths by defect
nodes.description: Encode the exploration events to bound the number of genuine two-generator path classes of length m and defect δ. The bound includes the endpoint colors and the corrected δ + 2 event budget.
nodes.map_note: Explicit class count at each defect

nodes.label: Bound each path's coefficients
nodes.description: First- and last-occurrence contractions bound each refined path's operator coefficient sum. For local dimension D, v visited vertices, e₁ singleton edges, integer defect δ, and moment order p, the repaired accounting gives exponent 9δ + 11.

nodes.label: One-pair moment comparison
nodes.description: The corrected class and coefficient bounds compare real normalized vacuum trace moments for one independent Haar pair, with finite matrix coefficients and remaining free-group factors. This is the version used by the prescribed-channel construction: p ≥ 2 and actual local dimension D = N + 1 ≥ 2⁸⁰p⁸⁰.
nodes.formula: Real Haar trace moment ≤ real free trace moment + D^(−1/2) ‖fregular‖ᵖ

nodes.label: Replace all tensor legs
nodes.description: For an even moment order p ≥ 2, apply the one-pair trace comparison successively to distinct tensor legs, then bound the expected operator norm by the free-regular norm times an explicit moment correction. The correction accounts for the enlarged matrix dimensions and remaining free coordinates.

nodes.label: Expected norm at prescribed size
nodes.description: At the manuscript's explicit local dimension and moment order, compare each admissible self-adjoint linear polynomial's Haar expected operator norm with its free-regular norm. The multiplicative error is explicitly controlled by K, n, and the coefficient dimension, supplying the expectation premise for finite sample selection.

nodes.label: One test controls a finite net
nodes.description: Build a symmetric 1/n net of normalized traceless observables and encode all of its tests into one self-adjoint linear polynomial. The coefficient-size budget and error transfer make a favorable polynomial sample control every test on the net.
nodes.map_note: One polynomial controls the whole net

nodes.label: Uniform adjoint certificate
nodes.description: Given the Haar expectation comparison, select one finite Haar sample and extend its finite-net estimate to every traceless Hermitian observable. The resulting block channel obeys a uniform operator-to-Hilbert–Schmidt bound, with κ = (n + 1)/(n − 1).
nodes.map_note: Uniform bound on the channel adjoint

nodes.label: All outputs have high entropy
nodes.description: Trace duality converts the uniform adjoint bound with constant t into a purity bound for every actual output density matrix of dimension d. It then bounds von Neumann entropy in nats from below.
nodes.formula: purity ≤ 1/d + t²; S_nats(output) ≥ ln d − ln(1 + dt²)

nodes.label: Bell input lowers joint entropy
nodes.description: An explicit tensor product of Bell states supplies a low-entropy output for the block complementary channel paired with its conjugate. The bound is in nats and holds for any finite local unitary family of K branches.
nodes.formula: S_nats(joint output) ≤ n(2 ln K − ln K/K)
nodes.map_note: Bell input gives low joint entropy

nodes.label: Turn entropy bounds into a gap
nodes.description: Apply the switch channel and Weyl extension to the base block channel. The adjoint certificate with constant t bounds single-use Holevo information, while the Bell witness gives a two-use lower bound for the same converted channel; both bounds here are in nats.
nodes.formula: χ_nats(T) ≤ ln(1 + Kⁿt²); χ_nats(T⊗T) ≥ n ln K/K

nodes.label: Prescribed channel and Holevo gap
nodes.description: Construct one finite CPTP channel with din = 2NⁿK^(2n), dout = Kⁿ, and N = ⌈exp(40(7 ln K + 2)n)⌉. In bits, the same witness has 2n/K ≤ χ(T) ≤ n log₂(1 + 9/K) + 2 log₂ κ and χ(T⊗T) ≥ n log₂ K/K, where κ = (n + 1)/(n − 1); assume only K ≥ 2 and n ≥ n₀(K).
nodes.formula: χ_bits(T⊗T) − 2χ_bits(T) ≥ n[log₂ K/K − 2 log₂(1 + 9/K)] − 4 log₂ κ

nodes.label: Keep chronological counting weights
nodes.description: Weight the actual exploration codes instead of replacing them by a padded-list count. The bound retains the event positions and the corrected δ + 2 budget, providing the sharper summation needed for the original moment threshold.

nodes.label: Sum weighted path contributions
nodes.description: Combine chronological class counts with the refined Haar path weights to bound the normalized sum of all active paths by a common coefficient scale times the displayed factor. This estimate assumes p ≥ 2, length 1 ≤ t ≤ p, and actual local dimension D = N + 1 ≥ 2³²p⁸⁰.
nodes.map_note: Sum active paths with sharper weights

nodes.label: Control each mixed word length
nodes.description: Insert the corrected coefficient estimate into the sharp normalized path sum and identify it with the actual mixed-moment contribution at each length 1 ≤ t ≤ p. The comparison is against the free-regular operator norm for finite matrix/free-factor polynomials.

nodes.label: Recover the original moment range
nodes.description: For p ≥ 2, sum the mixed-length contributions to compare the real normalized vacuum trace moments under actual local dimension D = N + 1 ≥ 2³²p⁸⁰. This strengthened endpoint is a separate route; the prescribed-channel proof references the 2⁸⁰ version.
nodes.formula: Real Haar trace moment ≤ real free trace moment + D^(−1/2) ‖fregular‖ᵖ

nodes.label: Build codes achieving Holevo rates
nodes.description: Lift each finite output ensemble to actual channel inputs and construct codes with normalized POVM decoders and vanishing Born error. Optimizing over these ensembles proves that single-use Holevo information in bits is an achievable capacity lower bound.

nodes.label: Convert block codes to all lengths
nodes.description: Flatten Kraus coordinates and pad inputs so a code for a positive tensor power becomes a physical code sequence at every sufficiently large length. The conversion preserves decoding error and accounts for the block-length rate factor.
nodes.map_note: Physical codes at all block lengths

nodes.label: Bound every finite code's messages
nodes.description: For an actual code with M messages, average error e, and output dimension d, POVM dilation and entropy continuity bound ln M by Holevo information in nats plus an explicit error correction. The estimate applies to arbitrary density-matrix encoders and normalized POVM decoders.
nodes.map_note: Message bound with explicit error term

nodes.label: Capacity equals regularized Holevo
nodes.description: Combine HSW achievability and physical blocking with the vanishing-error weak converse. Operational capacity, independently defined from real codes, equals the supremum of the normalized positive-power Holevo quantities.

nodes.label: Operational gain at prescribed size
nodes.description: Apply the capacity identity to the same prescribed channel to turn its two-use Holevo separation into an operational capacity gain in bits, with κ = (n + 1)/(n − 1). The exact dimensions, positive χ, and χ ≥ 2n/K are retained.
nodes.formula: C_bits(T) − χ_bits(T) ≥ n[log₂ K/K − 2 log₂(1 + 9/K)]/2 − 2 log₂ κ

nodes.label: Choose the growing block length
nodes.description: Set nK = ⌈K/√(ln K)⌉ and show that rounding does not change its leading scale. This choice balances decreasing single-use information against increasing two-use information as K grows.

nodes.label: Meet the construction threshold
nodes.description: Prove that the rounded nK eventually exceeds n₀(K), the threshold required by the prescribed-channel theorem. Therefore the actual growing family eventually uses precisely the intended block length.

nodes.label: Bounds for the actual growing family
nodes.description: Apply the prescribed bounds at nK = ⌈K/√(ln K)⌉ to the same selected finite channels. In bits, their single-use information is at least 2nK/K and at most nK log₂(1 + 9/K) plus the finite-size correction, while half their two-use information satisfies the displayed lower bound.
nodes.formula: 2nK/K ≤ χ_bits(TK); χ_bits(TK⊗TK)/2 ≥ nK ln K/(2K ln 2)
nodes.map_note: One- and two-use bounds for one family

nodes.label: Count the actual input qubits
nodes.description: Take log₂ of the selected channels' exact input dimensions, including the integer ceiling in the local dimension. Their input-qubit count qin is asymptotically quadratic in K with an explicit leading constant.

nodes.label: Translate K into input-qubit cost
nodes.description: Compare √(log₂ qin) with √(ln K) for the actual growing family. The explicit two-sided bounds transfer the information estimates from the parameter K to the physical input-qubit count.
nodes.map_note: Translate K into actual input-qubit cost

nodes.label: Information and capacity versus input cost
nodes.description: For the same growing family, both half the two-use Holevo information and operational capacity, in bits, are at least a positive constant times √(log₂ qin). Here qin is the actual input-qubit count and L = √(2/ln 2).

presets.label: Prescribed-channel construction
presets.description: Follow the corrected Haar moments and free comparison into a finite adjoint certificate, then combine output entropy with the Bell witness. This is the actual proof route used by the main prescribed-dimension theorem.

presets.label: Sharp Haar moment estimate
presets.description: The separate chronological weighted-counting route proves the one-pair estimate at D ≥ 2³²p⁸⁰. It shares the repaired exploration and coefficient estimates, while the main prescribed-channel route uses the 2⁸⁰ threshold.

presets.label: Operational capacity gain
presets.description: Combine the prescribed channel with a coding theorem proved from actual codewords, POVMs, and vanishing error. The conclusion is a gain C(T) − χ(T) for that channel.

presets.label: Growing-family input-qubit cost
presets.description: Choose nK = ⌈K/√(ln K)⌉, verify the construction threshold, and translate the same channels' information bounds into their actual input-qubit count. The cost is quadratic in K, while half the two-use information and capacity grow at least as √(log₂ qin).
